service.description: desired state: a program that should be running. It rides the same entity its `process` lands on — the service says what is wanted, the process says what is, and `stop` beside it says the wanting is over

command.description: the command line to run, argv joined by a space — the supervisor's own copy, kept here rather than read back off the process, because relaunching needs what we said and not what the kernel remembers

cwd.description: where to run it; absent means the supervisor's own cwd

restart.description: what to do when it ends, in systemd's three words; absent means never, so an unstated row runs once and stays down

attempts.description: how many times the supervisor has respawned it after an ending — the backoff climbs with this number, and a run that outlives the longest backoff starts the tally over

process.description: a program running on a host, tracked by pid — whether or not we started it

pid.description: the process id, on the host that tracks it — the one durable handle an adopted process has

command.description: the command line as launched, argv joined by a space; absent when the process was adopted rather than started here

cwd.description: where it was launched; absent for the same reason as command

exit.description: the process is over — never rewritten, and cleared only by the batch that lands the next attempt on a supervised row

code.description: the status it reported; absent when the ending was witnessed but the code was not (a signal took the wrapper, or nobody was watching)
